Dear Arthur,

I want to use your gl.drop.loc function on dartR data than someone send me in genlight but the @other.loc.metrics is NULL.
I only have the loc.names than I could used to drop loci potentially identfied under selection.

What do you advice me to use your function with loc.names ?

My data:
/// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////

 // 319 genotypes,  57,535 binary SNPs, size: 11.7 Mb
 658413 (3.59 %) missing data

 // Basic content
   @gen: list of 319 SNPbin

 // Optional content
   @ind.names:  319 individual labels
   @loc.names:  57535 locus labels
   @chromosome: factor storing chromosomes of the SNPs
   @position: integer storing positions of the SNPs
   @pop: population of each individual (group size range: 8-97)
   @other: a list containing: elements without names

messages.subject: Re: Keep specifed loci from a genelight object
parts:
Hi Nat,

We have done a rather substantial update of dartR, but it remains in beta version because it is not quite ready to upload to CRAN. People who agreed to beta test it have found some issues that we are progressively fixing.

Your best option is to download the latest version of dartR as per the instructions below:

install.packages("leaflet.providers")
install.packages("lifecycle")
install.packages("farver")
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR", ref="dev") # no need to upgrade prior installs, answer no.

Then you need to load the two attached scripts into your editor window and run them.

Run the compliance check on your genlight object using

gl <- gl.compliance.check(gl)

This will identify any issues, like @other.loc.metrics being NULL, and correct them.

Then you should be right to go.

Arthur
